editorial.headline: Fitness Clubs: Nationally Open, but Closed to PMA Registration in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This fitness-club activity is nationally open to full foreign ownership, yet a foreigner cannot register it at a Bali address under the province-wide PMA moratorium.
editorial.body:
KBLI 93127 covers professional, semi-professional and amateur fitness and bodybuilding clubs organised to give their members the opportunity to take part in sport. The defining activity is the club’s role in enabling participation, rather than a particular level of competition or a single physical format. It includes organisations that provide a place and facilities for sport, as well as those that do not.

The activity is open across small, medium and large business scales. That matters because the classification accommodates a club model at more than one size, while keeping the focus on access for members to sporting activity. A fitness or bodybuilding club may therefore fall within this scope whether its organisation is professional, semi-professional or amateur, provided that its purpose remains the opportunity for members to participate in sport.

At national level, the position is clear: the activity is open to foreign investment, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. The national framework cited in the record is Presidential Regulations 10/2021 and 49/2021. In other words, the national classification does not impose a foreign-equity cap below full ownership for this activity.

For a Bali address, however, a foreigner cannot register this activity today. Bali treats it as closed under its PMA moratorium because the large-business scale is classified as medium-low risk. The provincial rule blocks all low- and medium-low-risk KBLI activities from PMA registration across the island, on a permanent basis. This is not a reduction of the national 100% ownership ceiling; it is a Bali-specific bar on PMA registration for the activity, reflected in the Governor’s letter of May 2026.
